edition_scope: English Rules 2.0 (2016), including zero-survivor erratum; complete 6–12 player base game
verdict_basis: Read the complete frozen candidate and complete authoritative extracted text, and visually re-inspected all eight source pages for this candidate. No materially inaccurate claim or omission of a supplied important procedure was found. The added Blue4/Purple3 example, failed Emerald Ambush, restricted Blue retaliation and no runner-up promotion all agree with the page 7 diagram and text. Source gaps remain separately disclosed; PASS concerns fidelity, not completeness of the authoritative source as an executable specification.

checked_claims.claim: Title, designers, 6–12 players and 45–60 minute duration
12 IDs and stands, 12 sets of 12 voting cards, 11 target cards plus own-color Ambush per set, two three-card Showdown sets
80 gold cards with 26×3, 43×4, 11×5 point distribution; a bar is a card rather than a fixed point amount
Setup: visible upright IDs, matching voting sets, unused colors removed, own Ambush retained, face-down gold deck, four hidden-value central cards and Showdown sets aside
Rounds comprise repeated conspiracy and simultaneous voting among survivors; all players return for next round
One survivor takes four central bars; two survivors enter Final Showdown
Zero survivors: players absent from last vote each receive one deck card; final voters receive none; four central cards remain and no new central gold is added
Conspire before every vote for approximately 90 seconds maximum; any covert or overt communication
Game owner calls final decisions; one face-down card in front of its player; no turn order; changes until simultaneous reveal
Ambush cards are excluded from the tally; highest vote total determines Targets, including every highest-total tie
Targets and players who voted for no Target are eliminated subject to successful Ambush; knock down eliminated IDs
Successful Ambush requires being a Target, protects that player, and eliminates one player who voted for that ambusher
Ambush by a non-Target eliminates its own player; it does not add a vote or change another player’s Target eligibility
Three-player example: Red Ambush, Yellow votes Red, Pink votes Yellow; Red/Yellow tied; Red protected, Yellow eliminated, Red/Pink survive
Larger example: Blue receives four votes, Purple three; Blue alone is Target
Larger example: voters for Purple are eliminated for failing to vote for sole Target Blue; Emerald’s Ambush fails because Emerald is not Target
Larger example: Blue’s Ambush protects Blue; Blue chooses a voter for Blue, not an arbitrary player, to eliminate
Successful Ambush does not recalculate original vote totals or promote runner-up Purple to Target
checked_claims.result: SUPPORTED_BY_EXPLICIT_EXAMPLE: page 7 retains Blue as Target despite protection; surviving Blue voters and eliminated Purple voter group demonstrate original tally remains controlling.

checked_claims.claim: Each finalist takes one set of Share/Steal/Grab One & Go, discusses intentions, chooses face down and reveals simultaneously
Share/Share = 2/2
Share/Steal = 0/4; reverse = 4/0
Share/Grab One & Go = 3/1; reverse = 1/3
Steal/Grab One & Go = 3/1; reverse = 1/3
Steal/Steal = 0/0 finalists; every other player gets one deck card; four central cards remain
Grab One & Go/Grab One & Go = 1/1; two central cards remain and only two new cards added for ordinary next round
Other Showdown pairings distribute all four cards; ordinary continuing rounds restore central pool to four using hidden-value cards
Victory check after rewards at end of every round outcome; at least 25 points with 6–9 players or 24 with 10–12
Highest qualifying total wins; tied highest leaders conduct repeated extra Showdowns until a single table player has highest total
Extra Showdowns use ordinary pairing outcomes and outsider deck rewards; all table totals are compared and double-Steal reward may give an outsider the sole highest total
checked_claims.result: SUPPORTED_INFERENCE: page 4 requires another Final Showdown until any single table player has highest total; page 8 gives every non-finalist one deck card for double-Steal, with no tiebreak exception.

pdf_inspection.method: Opened the complete PDF with pypdf; read the complete authoritative extracted text and visually inspected all eight supplied source page images. All images were reopened for this candidate, with particular attention to page 5 vote instructions, page 7 full vote diagram and page 8 matrix. Earlier inspection established that PDF page 5 has no embedded text; visual evidence is essential.

source_executability_assessment.ordinary_positive_vote_two_finalist_play: Ordinary voting, successful and unsuccessful Ambush, and two-player payouts are supported. Unresolved edge cases and implicit component procedures are distinguished below.

source_gaps.trigger: Every surviving player plays Ambush, resulting in no counted votes.
source_gaps.gap: The booklet does not define whether zero votes produce no Target or everyone tied as Target. Under the latter reading successful Ambush has no eligible attacking voter to eliminate. No determinate procedure is supplied.
source_gaps.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no invented official resolution.
source_gaps.resolution_needed: Publisher ruling on zero-vote Target determination, Ambush outcome and survivor count.

source_gaps.trigger: Three or more players tie for highest qualifying gold total.
source_gaps.gap: Tied players are directed to another Showdown, but the only components and procedure support two participants. No multiway pairing or order is specified.
source_gaps.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed; no invented multiway procedure.
source_gaps.resolution_needed: Publisher method for three-or-more tied leaders, including order and subsequent total comparisons.

source_gaps.trigger: An extra game-end tie Showdown is required, potentially repeatedly.
source_gaps.gap: No pot size, card source or provisioning time is stated for immediate extra tie Showdowns. Previous round payouts may leave zero, two or four central cards. Ordinary next-round notes do not expressly resolve this immediate tiebreak supply issue.
source_gaps.summary_treatment: Explicitly disclosed. Same Showdown payout rules and deck rewards are retained without inventing a pot supply procedure.
source_gaps.resolution_needed: Publisher instruction defining the pot and any replenishment for each extra tie Showdown.

source_gaps.trigger: A later vote or round follows revealed voting/Ambush cards.
source_gaps.gap: Repeated voting with persistent sets implies reuse, but the source never expressly instructs returning revealed cards to owners or specifies recovery timing.
source_gaps.summary_treatment: Does not invent a discard, consumption or cost rule.
source_gaps.resolution_needed: Publisher sentence specifying revealed cards return to their owners before subsequent voting.

source_gaps.trigger: Differently valued hidden central gold is split between players or partly retained.
source_gaps.gap: Counts are fixed but selection/dealing of the specific awarded and retained cards is not specified; received-card inspection/publicity is also not fully stated beyond revealing a winning total.
source_gaps.summary_treatment: Preserves hidden central dealing and flags received-value publicity; supplies no invented draft/allocation rule.
source_gaps.resolution_needed: Publisher instructions for assigning specific cards and defining inspection/publicity of received gold.
